# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Repository Exploration Report: /app (Transaction Enrichment/Categorization Service)

## 1. Overall Repo Structure

This is a **Python 3.9 Flask microservice** for categorizing/enriching Indian bank statement transactions. Single git commit (`047782b import codebase`), branch `main`.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2 base, pip install -e ., gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore                          # notably ignores *.csv and TEST*.xml
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # setuptools; deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy,
    │                                   #   python-Levenshtein, scikit-learn, scipy, gunicorn
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app factory + request timing hooks
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP endpoints; giant per-bank if/elif dispatch (936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 per-bank categorizers (HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis, Kotak, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/             # shared regex constants, name cleaning, purpose, salary, PFM
```

- **Language/tooling:** Pure Python, pandas-vectorized rule engine (`np.select` over regex condition lists). No build system beyond `setup.py`; no lint config, no CI files.
- **Endpoints** (in `Controller.py`): `GET /`, `POST /recurrentTransactions`, `POST /categorizeTransaction` (takes `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`).
- **Runtime:** `Dockerfile` → `gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app`.

## 2. Transaction Categorization Logic (category from narration text)

The core pattern everywhere: lists of `[regex_condition_on_description, category]` pairs fed to `np.select`, defaulting to `"TRANSFER"`.

- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py`** — 35 files, one per bank; each exports `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)`. This is where `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `NEFT`, `IMPS`, `UPI`, `RTGS`, `ATM_WITHDRAWAL`, `CASH_DEPOSIT`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, `REVERSAL`, etc. are assigned. Representative example: `BankScripts/HDFC.py` lines 11–104 (e.g. line 58 `^UPI` → UPI, line 59 `IMPS-` → IMPS, line 60 `NEFT [CcDd][Rr]-` → NEFT, lines 71–75 `\bCHQ\b|Chq Paid|CHQ DEP` → CHEQUE_PAID/CHEQUE_DEPOSIT).
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`** — dispatch by `bank` string ("HDFC", "SBI", "ICICI", ... "PAYTM_BANK", "STANDARD_CHARTERED"), then chains: categorize → purpose → clean_names → internal_payment → salary_detection → PFM.
- **`UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py`** / **`TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py`** — enum-style catalogs of all category/subcategory values (incl. `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION="Account Verification"` at CategoryEnums line 83).
- **`UtilityScripts/Purpose.py`** — second-pass "purpose" assignment (SALARY, MEDICAL_EXPENSES, LOAN, etc.) on top of transactionCategory.
- **`UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py`**, **`SimpleDescription.py`** — PFM-facing category mapping and human-readable descriptions.
- **`UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py`**, **`RecurrentTxns.py`**, **`InternalPayment.py`** — salary inference (recurring credits), recurrent-txn grouping, self-transfer detection (fuzzy match vs accountHolder).
- **Credit-card flow:** `UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py`, `CardCleanNames.py`.

## 3. Counterparty Name Extraction (partyName)

Two layers:

- **Per-bank extraction inside each `BankScripts/*.py`** — after categorization, a `partyName` column is derived by splitting the narration on delimiters via helpers in **`UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`** (`sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_`, `sep_by_colon`, `sep_by_comma`, ... and `py_extract` for regex-group extraction). Examples:
  - `HDFC.py` lines 146–247: `^NEFT [CD][Rr]-<IFSC>-...` → token 3; `^UPI-` → token 1–2; `^IMPS-` → token 2; `CHQ PAID-` → dash tokens 3–4; cheque patterns HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1–10.
  - `Axis.py` line 145: `BRN-CLG-CHQ PAID TO <name>` extraction; `Citi.py` lines 119–143: `CHQ PAID Check ... TO (.*)`; `Central.py` lines 73–74: `CHQ PAID (.*) -` / `CHQ PAID-` dash split; `AuSmallFinanceBank.py` line 78: `^CHQ PAID-` dash tokens 1–2 (this is the family matching your "CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR" example).
- **`UtilityScripts/CleanName.py`** (1971 lines, `clean_names()`) — global normalization of extracted party names to canonical merchants ("Airtel DTH", "TataSky DTH", "Employee Provident Fund Organisation", etc.), plus junk stripping.
- **`UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py`** — same for credit-card narrations.
- **`UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`** — also `fuzzy_match()` (fuzzywuzzy) used by InternalPayment.

## 4. Test Fixtures / Baseline Corpus and Test Commands

**There are none in this repository.** Verified thoroughly:

- No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, conftest, pytest/unittest imports, tox/nox/Makefile, or CI config anywhere (`git ls-files` = 54 files, all listed above).
- No CSV/JSON fixture corpus — and `.gitignore` explicitly ignores `*.csv` and `TEST*.xml` ("Unit test reports"), which suggests fixture CSVs and JUnit-style reports existed in the original working environment but were deliberately excluded from version control.
- `setup.py` declares no test dependencies or `test_suite`.

**The only executable "verification" paths are running the service itself:**

```bash
# install
cd /app/categorizationapp && pip3 install -e .

# run (production style, matches Dockerfile)
cd /app/categorizationapp && gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app

# or via Docker
docker build -t categorizationapp /app && docker run -p 9898:9898 categorizationapp

# smoke test
curl -X POST localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"bank":"HDFC","acc_type":"SAVING","accountUID":"u1","accountHolder":"RAVI KUMAR","transactions":[...]}'
```

If you need a baseline corpus for regression testing, it will have to be created (or restored from wherever the ignored CSVs lived).

## 5. Regex / Rule Files (cheque, NEFT, IMPS, UPI, penny-drop)

Both are pure-Python constants modules — the closest thing to "rule files":

- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`** (432 lines) — bank-specific patterns. Highlights:
  - **Penny-drop / account verification:** `ACC_VERIF` (line 6, includes `pennyd`, `/bav`, `[0-9]/BV[0-9]`), `BANK_VER_HD` (line 75, HDFC: `pennydrop|/BAV-|TestVPA|BENE NAME...`), `BANK_VER_BOI` (line 110), `ACC_VERIFY_PNB` (133), `BANK_VERIF` (321), `ACC_VERIF_PAYTM` (428), `ACC_VERI_SCB` (431), plus per-bank `ACC_VERI_*` variants. Consumed in bank scripts combined with `amount in (1, -1)` / `amount < 2` guards.
  - **Cheque:** `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1`–`PATTERN10` (lines 81–90, e.g. `"Chq Paid-MICR CTS|CHQ PAID-MICR CTS"`, `"CHQ DEP - .* - MICR.*:(.*):"`), generic `CHQ_PATTERN1`–`4` (lines 314–317, `MICR INWARD...`).
  - **NEFT:** `NEFT_PATTERN0`–`7` (206–213), `UB_NEFT_1_UNION`–`8` (120–128), `NEFT_CLEAN_KOTAK` (214), `NEFT_PAYMENT_STOP`/`NEFT_DEBIT_STOP` (333–334, IFSC-prefix stoplists).
  - **IMPS:** `IMPS_PATTERN1`–`8` (195–202), `RCVD_FROM_IMPS1`–`5` (234–238), `SBI_IMPS_1`–`3` (60–62).
  - **RTGS:** `UB_RTGS_*` (128–129), `PNB_RTGS_KEYWORDS`/`PNB_RTGS_1` (151–152), `KT_RTGS_PATTERN`/`RTGS_PATTERN1` (217–218).
  - Also per-bank charges/reversal stoplists (`BANK_CHARGES_HDFC`, `CHARGE_YES`, `REVERSAL_RBL`, ...).
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py`** (191 lines) — cross-bank semantic lexicons: `SALARY`, `LOAN_REP*`, `CREDIT_CARD`, `SHOPPING`, `UTILITY`, `INSURANCE`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`/`INSUFF_BOUNCE` (cheque-return reason regexes, lines 86–87), `TDS`, `PAYMENT_GATEWAY`, `SAL_IMPS`, etc.
- Additional **inline regexes live directly in each `BankScripts/*.py`** (e.g., UPI handling is mostly inline: HDFC `"^UPI|UPI-?\s?"` line 58; Axis `"^IMPS/"` party split line 123; cheque-number style match HDFC line 100: 16-char remark `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT).

Since the whole tree is one commit, no file is "more recent" than another per git; recency of rules can't be inferred from history.

arguments.prompt:
You are auditing a Python transaction-categorization codebase at /app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/. Each bank script builds `partyName` via np.select over [condition, choice] rule lists, using helpers sep_by_(desc,n1,n2) (split on "/"), sep_by_dash (split on "-"), sep_by_colon (split on ":"), and py_extract(desc, pat, index) (regex group extract; returns "" if group index doesn't exist).

Context: A QA report says two regressions exist somewhere in these scripts:
(A) An inbound IMPS (instant payment, P2P/P2A) CREDIT ends up with partyName = a bare numeric reference number (a fragment of the narration/reference string) instead of the sender's name. Neighbouring IMPS layouts in the same bank still extract names correctly. Note: many banks have post-cleanup rules that blank out partyName values that are all digits (e.g. `^[0-9]+$`, `^[0-9]{4,}$`, `^[0-9]{2,}`) — in the buggy bank, the numeric value SURVIVES to the final output, so the bank either lacks such a numeric-blanking cleanup or the cleanup doesn't cover this case.
(B) Possibly related: an inbound NEFT credit layout yields a blank name (I already suspect PNB.py line 110 `py_extract(pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` — a 1-group pattern extracted with index=1 always yields blank. You can confirm or find better candidates.)

Task: Read EVERY file in /app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ that I list below (these are the ones not yet fully audited): YES.py, Federal.py, Indian.py, Central.py, BOI.py, Bandhan.py, ICICI.py, DCB.py, CityUnion.py, Andhra.py, SVC.py, Citi.py, Karnataka.py, Saraswat.py, SouthIndian.py, UCO.py, UnionBank.py, Syndicate.py, TamilnadMerchantile.py, Paytm.py, IDBI.py, Indusind.py, StandardCharted.py, BankOfMaharashtra.py, BOB.py, KarurVyasa.py, IDFC.py, Axis.py, SBI.py, HDFC.py.

For each, look at the IMPS and NEFT partyName extraction rules AND the subsequent partyName cleanup np.select blocks. Identify any rule where:
1. The token index / regex group extracted would plausibly grab the numeric reference/RRN (12-digit) token instead of the name token, judging by the surrounding rules for the same bank (e.g., a sibling rule for a near-identical layout uses index N but this one uses N-1), AND
2. The bank's cleanup passes would NOT blank a purely numeric partyName.

Also flag any py_extract call whose `index` exceeds the number of capture groups in its pattern (always-blank bugs), and any obviously inconsistent index in IMPS/NEFT rule families.

Report: for each finding, file:line, the rule, why it's inconsistent with its siblings, and whether numeric partyName survives that bank's cleanup. Be precise; quote the code. Do NOT modify any files - research only.

<task id="ses_02c4e7ff4ffeANyDQfFRkqn3zQ" state="completed">
<task_result>
All 30 listed files read, plus PNB.py, Canara.py, the helpers (`AppUtil.py`) and `BankRegexConstants.py`. I also ran a repo-wide automated scan of every `py_extract` call (resolving constant-name patterns) for `index >= number-of-groups`, and checked file metadata since git history is a single squashed commit.

# Key forensic fact

`git log` shows one commit, but file mtimes differ: **every bank script is dated Nov 2 2022 except `PNB.py` and `Canara.py` (both Jul 15 02:30)**. Both QA regressions are consistent with a single edit to **PNB.py** ("possibly related" — indeed, same file).

---

## Finding B (CONFIRMED): PNB.py:110 — always-blank NEFT extraction

```python
[transactions.transactionCategory.ne("CHARGES") & transactions.description.str.contains("^NEFT ", na=False, case=False)           , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)],
```

- `"NEFT (.*)"` has **1 capture group**; `str.extract(...).get(1)` returns `None`, and `py_extract` (AppUtil.py:61-66) then returns `pd.Series("")` — **unconditionally blank**.
- It's the final fallback of the NEFT family, so any inbound credit like `NEFT PUNBH12345678901 JOHN DOE` that misses the earlier layout-specific rules (PNB.py:97-109) gets a blank name.
- Every sibling in the same block uses `index=0` for 1-group patterns (e.g. PNB.py:104 `pat="NEFT_IN:NEFT/"…`, PNB.py:120 `pat=PNB_RTGS_1, index=0`). The only legitimate `index=1` calls in the repo are on 2-group patterns (ICICI.py:159, ICICI.py:168, DCB.py:80-81, BankOfMaharashtra.py:126, SBI.py:139/146/147 via `SBI_AUTOPAY7/8/9`).
- My automated scan confirms **PNB.py:110 is the only `py_extract` in the entire BankScripts directory whose index exceeds its pattern's group count**:
  ```
  PNB.py:110: index=1 but pattern has 1 group(s): 'NEFT (.*)'
  ```

Fix direction: `index=0` (and preferably anchor past the UTR: `"^NEFT [A-Z0-9]+ (.*)"`).

## Finding A: PNB.py:94-95 — inbound IMPS P2A credit gets the numeric reference token, and PNB has no numeric-blanking cleanup

```python
92:    conditions_choices = [
93:        #imps
94:        [transactions.description.str.contains("^IMPSOUTP2A", na=False, case=False)                        , sep_by_(transactions.description,2,3)],
95:        [transactions.transactionCategory.eq("IMPS") & transactions.description.str.contains("^IMPS", na=False, case=False), sep_by_(transactions.description,3,4)],
```

Why this is the inconsistency:

1. **Near-identical layouts, different indices.** `IMPSOUTP2A/<12-digit RRN>/<NAME>/<ref>` and the inbound twin `IMPSINP2A/<12-digit RRN>/<NAME>/<ref>` have identical slash-token structure (`IMPSIN`/`IMPSOUT` is explicitly recognized in this bank's categorizer — PNB.py:51 `"\\bIMPS\\b|^IMPSOUT|^IMPSIN"`). The outbound rule (line 94) takes slash-token **2** — the name. There is **no `^IMPSINP2A` rule**; inbound credits fall through to the generic line 95, which takes slash-token **3** — the field *after* the name, i.e. the trailing narration/reference fragment (typically the numeric ref/RRN echo). Result: partyName = a bare numeric reference string, exactly the QA symptom. Meanwhile "neighbouring IMPS layouts still extract names correctly": outbound P2A via line 94, and 4-token `IMPS/P2A/<RRN>/<NAME>` layouts genuinely have the name at token 3, so line 95 is right for those — only the `IMPSINP2A/...` single-prefix inbound layout lands on the wrong token.
2. **Numeric survives PNB's cleanup — uniquely.** PNB's partyName cleanup (PNB.py:169-184) blanks only `^Na$|^Tr$|^Chq$|^Ca$|^Cc$|^Trfr?$|^Amt Trf To` (line 177) and does cosmetic strips. **There is no digits-only blanking rule anywhere in PNB.** Contrast with the banks QA cited as having such passes:
   - BOB.py:151 `"^[0-9]+$|^N[Aa]$|^[A-Za-z]$|[0-9]{5,}"` → ""
   - Axis.py:168 `"...|^[0-9]{4,}$|..."` → ""
   - Karnataka.py:92 `"...|^[0-9]{2,}|..."` → ""
   - Canara.py:174 `"...|^[0-9]{5,}"` → "" ; ICICI.py:233 `"[0-9]{6,}|..."` → "" ; HDFC.py:261 blanks any name with no letters; SBI.py:161 strips leading digits.

   So a 12-digit value produced in PNB reaches final output untouched (line 167/188 only `strip().title()`).

Fix direction: add the inbound sibling mirroring line 94, e.g. `^IMPSINP2A → sep_by_(2,3)`.

---

## Secondary / latent findings (pre-existing — files unmodified since 2022 — but they match your criteria and are worth logging)

1. **Canara.py:127** — `[^IMPS: ...] , sep_by_colon(transactions.description,1,2)`. For `IMPS:<RRN>:<NAME>` this grabs colon-token 1 = the RRN. Its own sibling on line 126 (`^IMPS:.*~`) strips **all digits and colons** from the same prefix family (proving digits precede the name), and the `^RTGS:` siblings (Canara.py:114-115) take the *last* colon token (2,3 / 3,4). However, Canara.py:174 blanks `^[0-9]{5,}`, so a clean 12-digit value is caught by cleanup — it does **not** survive, which is why this is not QA finding (A).
2. **Federal.py:81** — `[^IMPS/IFO/ ...] , sep_by_(transactions.description,4,5)` vs sibling **Federal.py:80** `[^FT IMPS/IFO/ ...] , sep_by_(3,4)`. The `FT ` prefix contains no `/`, so both layouts tokenize identically — the two indices cannot both be right. Federal has **no partyName cleanup block at all** (Federal.py:108 → 111 goes straight to `party2`), so whichever rule is off-by-one, a numeric/reference token survives. Off-by-one within the IFO family; flagged as inconsistent-index candidate.
3. **Syndicate.py:69** — `[^IMPS: ...] , sep_by_colon(1,2)`: same shape as Canara.py:127; if Syndicate's `IMPS:` layout is `IMPS:<RRN>:<NAME>`, this yields the RRN, and Syndicate's cleanups (lines 119-136) blank digits only for CARD_PAYMENT/ONLINE_PAYMENT (line 123) — an IMPS numeric would survive. Pre-existing, but structurally identical to symptom (A).
4. **UnionBank.py:100** — malformed rule row:
   ```python
   [transactions.description.str.contains("^UPI/[CD]R/[0-9]+/", na=False, case=False) & sep_by_dash(transactions.description,3,4)],
   ```
   `&` where a `,` belongs — the row has one element, so the DataFrame's `choices` becomes `None` (verified: construction does not raise; the row silently gets `choices=None`). It's also shadowed by line 99 (`^UPI` catch-all), so it's dead/latent, but it's a genuine defect.
5. **YES.py:113-114** — the `#imps` section of the partyName block is **empty** (all YES IMPS transactions get blank partyName by default), and **KarurVyasa.py** likewise has no IMPS partyName rules. Blank, not numeric — noted for completeness.
6. **BankOfMaharashtra.py:182** — `py_extract(pat="([0-9]{9})", index=0)` deliberately sets a 9-digit number as partyName for `ADM…TO INGENICO` auto-payments; BoM has no digits-only blanking, so this numeric persists — but it appears intentional (merchant ref) and is a DEBIT auto-pay, not IMPS.

## Bottom line

- **(A)** = `PNB.py:95` (missing/wrong-index inbound sibling of `PNB.py:94`): inbound `IMPSINP2A/<RRN>/<name>/<numeric ref>` credits get slash-token 3 (numeric reference) instead of token 2 (sender name), and PNB's cleanup (PNB.py:169-184) contains no digits-only blanking, so the number survives to output.
- **(B)** = `PNB.py:110`, confirmed: `py_extract(pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` on a 1-group pattern is always blank — the only such overflow in the whole directory.
- Both sit in `PNB.py`, one of only two files modified after the original import (the other, `Canara.py`, contains the structurally similar but cleanup-neutralized `^IMPS:` issue at line 127).

No files were modified.

steps.message:
All five findings are cleared. Root-causing first: file mtimes show every bank script dates from the original 2022 import except `PNB.py` and `Canara.py` (both touched 2026-07-15), so all regressions had to live in those two files — which is exactly where the defects were.

**Fixes (one per finding):**

- **F-1** — `BankScripts/PNB.py:60`: the DEBIT-side bare-cheque-number rule read remark `^[0-9]{5}$` while its own CREDIT twin on line 61 reads `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. Standard 6-digit cheque numbers on debits fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Restored to `{5,6}`.
- **F-2** — `BankScripts/Canara.py:165`: `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` was handled by the generic `^CHQ PAID-` rule taking dash tokens 1–2 (`MICR CLG`, the clearing tag). Added a dedicated `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-` rule taking tokens 2–3 (the payee name), mirroring the adjacent `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` rule; the generic rule stays intact for single-dash `CHQ PAID-<name>` layouts.
- **F-3** — `BankScripts/PNB.py:111`: the fallback NEFT-credit name rule was `py_extract(pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` — a one-group pattern read at group index 1, which `py_extract` turns into an unconditional blank (verified it was the only such group-overflow in the whole repo). Now extracts the name after the UTR token: `^NEFT [A-Za-z]*[0-9]+[A-Za-z0-9]* (.*)`, index 0. Since the old rule produced only blanks, no currently-correct row can shift.
- **F-4** — `BankScripts/PNB.py:95`: outbound `^IMPSOUTP2A` takes slash-token 2 (the name), but there was no inbound twin, so `IMPSINP2A/<RRN>/<name>/<ref>` credits fell to the generic IMPS rule taking token 3 — the trailing reference number — and PNB has no digits-only partyName cleanup to catch it. Added `^IMPSINP2A` → token 2 ahead of the generic rule.
- **F-5** — `BankScripts/Canara.py:19`: the penny-drop guard was `amount.lt(1)`, which excludes the canonical ₹1 verification credit (every other bank uses `lt(2)`, `eq(1)`, or `isin([1,-1])`). Restored to `lt(2)`; sub-rupee rows behave exactly as before.

**Verification:** replayed synthetic fixtures through `categorize_PNB_transactions` and `categorize_Canara_transactions` — all five regressed forms now derive their baseline category/name (`CHEQUE_PAID`, `Ravi Kumar`, `Reliance Retail Ltd`, `Ravi Kumar` via IMPSINP2A, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`), while guard rows covering the neighbouring layouts (5-digit remarks, credit-side cheque deposits, `NEFT_IN:-` layout, `IMPSOUTP2A`, 4-token `IMPS/P2A`, Home-Clearing cheques, single-dash cheques, sub-rupee verifications, ordinary deposits/transfers) are byte-identical to their prior output. Each fix is scoped so only rows currently deriving the wrong value can change.
